newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey April inflation expected between 5-5.5 pct. [CORRECTED 15:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Turkey April inflation expected between 5-5.5 pct. [CORRECTED 15:23 GMT]

text.p: Turkish market analysts said on Friday they expect the wholesale and consumer price index to increase by around 5 to 5.5 percent in April.
In April 1996 (corrects from Last year) the wholesale price index increased by 8.1 percent and the consumer price index was up by 6.7 percent.
"We are expecting 5.4 percent WPI and 5.3 percent CPI for April," said Altug Karamenderes, analyst at Ata Securities Inc.

Karamenderes said the main inflationary data, money supply and the central bank's interest rate strategy showed that there were no major structural changes under way which might modify these expectations.

Another said the dynamics of the core inflation data was unchanged and the approach of the summer season, which usually heralds low inflation, gave reason to believe that April inflation would not exceed five percent.
A few analysts were pessimistic on the main economic indicators and the uneasy state of the country's politics and said they expected index increases of more than six percent.
They said they were concerned about demand-induced inflation, fuelled by an increase in money supply and public sector price hikes.
The expected year-end inflation rate for 1997 is around 72-75 percent, bankers said.
